page: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Daldv6 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. This virtual machine is configured with 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores, utilizing Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization with two threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the instance includes 1890 GB of local storage and is premium storage capable, though it does not feature any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring 3081.05 in stress-ng and 2099.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, both placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 49279.31 and a PassMark CPU score of 46771.35. The system exhibits strong capabilities in specific workloads, such as bzip3 decompression (187.81 GB/sec multi-threaded) and PassMark CPU encryption (38565.36), which both rank in the top 25%. Memory performance is also strong, with a PassMark memory score of 2756.72, while large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 80.53 GB/sec.

For specialized workloads, the D32alds_v6 shows top-tier performance in text generation for small (135M) language models, achieving 344.97 tokens per second, alongside strong prompt processing at 2606.79 tokens per second. However, performance scales down to average levels for larger models, such as 20.38 tokens per second for a 7B model. Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial 1890 GB local storage, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy tasks that require local scratch space but do not demand high memory density. It is well-suited for software compilation, image processing, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D32alds_v6 is an x86_64 server instance from the Daldv6 family, powered by a dedicated 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores), 64.0 GB of RAM, and 1890 GB of local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance offers a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a compute-focused option with integrated local disk capacity. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU performance, ranking in the top 25% for Geekbench and stress-ng, alongside strong memory performance and encryption capabilities. It also achieves top-tier text generation speeds for small language models. With its balanced compute power and local storage, the D32alds_v6 is suited for workloads such as software compilation, image and text processing, and lightweight model inference, offering qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense compute tasks that do not require high memory allocations.
